objectives.text: Singers have their parts ready before rehearsal
The choir spends no volunteer time keeping the service running

rejected.label: Syncs with the rehearsal calendar app
rejected.note: Provisional reading: the user did not say what the sync is for. It is treated as a way of getting parts ready for rehearsal, to be confirmed. Whether it is a hard requirement is asked in questions.

anchors.text: A source states that a singer must browse or search the whole library to reach their own part.
A source states that a singer can reach their own part from a personal folder, but must set that folder up first.
A source states that a singer can reach their own part in one step, with no set-up.

definition.objective: Singers have their parts ready before rehearsal
definition.question: How many steps does a singer take to reach their own part?
definition.evidenceRule: The vendor's documentation or product page describing how a singer opens a part; a reviewer's general praise does not count.

missingRules.when: No source describes how a singer reaches a part.
Sources disagree about how a singer reaches a part.

exclusions: How quickly the library loads or how it looks.
Syncs with the rehearsal calendar app: judge how fast a singer reaches their part, not the sync.

anchors.text: A source states that a volunteer must maintain the service every week.
A source states that a volunteer must maintain the service at set points in each season.
A source states that the service needs no volunteer action after its initial setup.

definition.objective: The choir spends no volunteer time keeping the service running
definition.question: What ongoing action does the service need from a volunteer, and how often?
definition.evidenceRule: A stated ongoing task, such as a recurring upload or check, in the vendor's documentation for an organisation account.

missingRules.when: No source describes the ongoing tasks the service needs.
Sources disagree about how often a volunteer must act.

exclusions: The subscription price; that is not volunteer time.

provenance.quote: Singers need to find their parts quickly before rehearsal.
We can't afford anything that needs a volunteer to maintain it every week.

questions: Cost is not mentioned. Is it a criterion for this decision, or already settled by a budget?
It must sync with the rehearsal calendar app. Is that a hard requirement, so that a service which cannot sync is ruled out whatever else it does? And what should the sync do for the singers?
Scorebox, Chorale Hub and FolioSing advertise dark mode or colour themes, and FolioSing advertises offline mode. Do any of these matter to you?

objectives.text: Mentors spend no evenings chasing orders

rejected.label: Branding
rejected.note: The user said: Forget about branding, we don't care.

rejected.label: Orders go through the school's purchase-order system
rejected.note: Provisional reading: the user did not say what the purchase-order route is for. It is treated as a way of keeping ordering out of mentors' evenings, to be confirmed. Whether it is a hard requirement is asked in questions.

anchors.text: A source states that stocked items take more than a week to dispatch or deliver.
A source states that stocked items ship within three working days.
A source states that stocked items ship the next day.

definition.question: How quickly does a stocked item reach the school after an order is placed?
definition.evidenceRule: A stated dispatch or delivery time in the vendor's own documentation or product page; a review's report of one late parcel does not count.

missingRules.when: No source states a dispatch or delivery time.
Sources give conflicting dispatch or delivery times.

exclusions: Whether an item is in stock at all; this criterion covers only how fast a stocked item arrives.
Order tracking: how a mentor follows an order; that is order-tracking.

anchors.text: A source states that order status can only be learned by contacting the supplier by email or phone.
A source states that order status can be seen online, but a delayed order needs the supplier contacted.
A source states that order status and delivery updates are sent to the buyer automatically, with no contact needed.

definition.objective: Mentors spend no evenings chasing orders
definition.question: Can a mentor learn where an order is without contacting the supplier?
definition.evidenceRule: The vendor's documentation of order status and updates for school or business accounts.

missingRules.when: No source describes how a buyer checks order status.
Sources conflict on whether order status is available online.

exclusions: Orders go through the school's purchase-order system: judge whether a mentor can follow an order, not the purchase route.

provenance.quote: We need parts to arrive before competition deadlines.
Mentors are volunteers and can't spend evenings chasing orders.

questions: Everything has to be ordered through the school's purchase-order system. Is that a hard requirement, so that a supplier which cannot be used that way is ruled out whatever else it does? And what is the purchase-order route for?
Loyalty points are advertised by all three suppliers. Is that the branding you have dropped, or do the points matter to you?
The delivery criterion covers stocked items only. Do you also need parts that are not in stock, and do those need to arrive by a deadline?
Cost is not mentioned. Is it a criterion, or already settled by a budget? Bulk discounts and school accounts are advertised by two suppliers.

objectives.text: Members borrow a tool without waiting days
The society knows who has each tool so nothing goes missing

rejected.label: Has a mobile app
rejected.note: Provisional reading: the user did not say what the mobile app is for. It is treated as a way for members to borrow without waiting, to be confirmed. Whether it is a hard requirement is asked in questions.

criteria.label: Time to borrow an available tool

anchors.text: A source states that a borrow request waits at least a few days for the owner or a librarian to approve it.
A source states that a borrow request is answered within one day.
A source states that an available tool can be borrowed at once, with no request step.

definition.objective: Members borrow a tool without waiting days
definition.question: How long must a member wait between asking for an available tool and having it?
definition.evidenceRule: The platform's documentation of the borrowing steps and their timing; a review's general praise does not count.

missingRules.when: No source describes how a borrow request is handled.
Sources disagree about how long a borrow request takes.

exclusions: Has a mobile app: judge how long a borrow takes, not which device is used.
Who holds each tool; that is who-holds-tool.

anchors.text: A source states that the platform records no borrower for lent tools.
A source states that the platform records borrowers, but only when a member chooses to log a loan.
A source states that every loan is recorded against the borrower, and that the current holder of each tool is shown.

definition.objective: The society knows who has each tool so nothing goes missing
definition.question: Does the platform show who currently holds each tool?
definition.evidenceRule: The platform's documentation of how loans are recorded and what is shown for a lent tool.

missingRules.when: No source describes how loans are recorded.
Sources disagree on whether loans are recorded automatically.

exclusions: Whether members return tools on time: the record shows who holds a tool, not whether it comes back.

provenance.quote: Members should be able to borrow a tool without waiting days.
We want to know who has which tool so nothing goes missing.

questions: It needs a mobile app. What is that for, and is it a hard requirement, so that a tool library without one is ruled out whatever else it does?
The three brochures advertise 9, 14 and 20 languages. Does the number of languages matter to you?
Cost is not mentioned. Is it a criterion for this decision, or already settled by a budget?

objectives.text: The group has the route before the walk

rejected.label: Social feed
rejected.note: The user said: Nobody cares about the social feed.

rejected.label: Exports GPX files
rejected.note: Provisional reading: the user did not say what GPX export is for. It is treated as a way of getting the route onto the group's own devices, to be confirmed. Whether it is a hard requirement is asked in questions.

criteria.label: Shares a route with the group in advance

anchors.text: A source states that a route can only be shared with one person at a time.
A source states that a route can be shared with a group, but each member must create an account first.
A source states that a route can be shared with a whole group in one step, at any time before the walk, with no account needed by members.

definition.objective: The group has the route before the walk
definition.question: Can a leader send a route to the whole group ahead of the walk, and what must each member do?
definition.evidenceRule: The app's documentation or product page describing how a route is shared; a review's praise for the feature does not count.

missingRules.when: No source describes how a route is shared.
Sources disagree on whether a route can be shared with a group.

exclusions: Exports GPX files: judge when and to whom a route can be shared, not the file format.
Route planning: how a route is built, not how it is passed on.

provenance.quote: Leaders need to share a route with the group the evening before.

questions: It has to export GPX files. Why, and is it a hard requirement, so that an app without GPX export is ruled out whatever else it does?
Badges, offline maps, elevation profiles and weather overlays are advertised, but you did not mention them. Do any of them matter?
Cost is not mentioned. Is it a criterion for this decision, or already settled by a budget?

objectives.text: Parents buy tickets in under a minute
Card payments can be taken at the door

rejected.label: Merchandise sales
rejected.note: The user said: Don't bother with merchandise sales.

anchors.text: A source states that buying a ticket requires creating an account before any seat can be chosen.
A source states that buyers can check out as guests, but must choose their seat across several screens.
A source states that a buyer can choose a seat and pay as a guest in one continuous flow.

definition.objective: Parents buy tickets in under a minute
definition.question: Can a parent choose a seat and pay, as a guest, in one continuous flow?
definition.evidenceRule: The vendor's documentation or product page describing the buying steps; a review's general praise does not count.

missingRules.when: No source describes the steps a buyer takes.
Sources disagree about whether guests can buy tickets.

exclusions: The look of the buying page; that is not how many steps it takes.

criteria.label: Takes card payments at the door

anchors.text: A source states that the system cannot take card payments at the door.
A source states that card payments at the door need a separate device or a separately bought app.
A source states that the door app takes card payments on the same device that scans tickets.

definition.objective: Card payments can be taken at the door
definition.question: Can the box office take a card payment at the door, and on what equipment?
definition.evidenceRule: The vendor's documentation of door sales; a brochure's mention of a door app counts only if it names card payment.

missingRules.when: No source describes door sales.
Sources disagree on whether door card payments are supported.

exclusions: Ticket scanning at the door without payment: a scanner that does not take payment does not meet this criterion.

anchors.text: A source states that seats are assigned by hand, with no check against existing sales.
A source states that the system checks seat availability for online sales, but not for door sales.
A source states that online and door sales draw on one seat record, so a sold seat cannot be sold again.

definition.question: Does one seat record stop a seat being sold through more than one channel?
definition.evidenceRule: The vendor's documentation of how seat sales are recorded across channels.

missingRules.when: No source describes how seat sales are recorded.
Sources disagree on whether seats are checked across channels.

exclusions: Seat maps and allocated seating layouts: how seats are displayed, not whether a sold seat is protected.

provenance.quote: Parents should be able to buy tickets in under a minute.
It has to take card payments at the door.
We are sick of double-booked seats.

questions: It has to take card payments at the door. Is that a hard requirement, so that a ticketing service without door card payments is ruled out whatever else it does?
Customisable colour themes are advertised by all three services. Do they matter to you?
Seat maps and allocated seating are advertised, but you did not raise them. Do parents need to choose their own seat?
Cost is not mentioned. Is it a criterion for this decision, or already settled by a budget?
